subject: Azure private plan — commercials, co-sell split & onboarding next steps
messages:
From: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cloudwave.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:02:00Z
Subject: Azure private listing inquiry + initial RFI

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudWave is definitely interested in listing Redwood under an Azure private plan for our enterprise customers in EMEA. Procurement asked me to share a short RFI and outline the items they need to progress:

- Proposed marketplace fee schedule (percent of net revenue) for private plans
- Co-sell revenue split mechanics and reporting cadence
- Any minimum reserved capacity or committed billing terms for private listings
- Data retention, logging and audit requirements (SOC2 / logging retention windows)
- Draft T&Cs / redlineable contract for Azure marketplace private offers

I've attached a short RFI that procurement will use to capture responses. Can you share a term sheet and the typical commercials you offer for private plans? Also, procurement asked whether Redwood will entertain a co-sell split in the 60/40 — 70/30 range (CloudWave share first).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline this month.

Attachments: CloudWave_Azure_RFI_08052026.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Matt
Matt Reynolds
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudWave
procure@cloudwave.com | +44 20 7123 4567

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cloudwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private listing inquiry + initial RFI

Matt — great to connect.

Thanks for the RFI. I'm attaching our standard private-plan term sheet to give procurement visibility into common constructs (marketplace fee assumptions, typical co-sell splits, and onboarding milestones). High level responses:

- Marketplace fee: Azure marketplace takes a platform fee — on top of that we typically model a gross-to-net split with partners. We can share modeled examples once we know expected ARR bands.
- Co-sell split: we have historically accepted 60/40 or 65/35 arrangements for strategic partners, subject to commit levels and joint GTM contribution.
- Reserved capacity: optional; many enterprise customers prefer a reserved block for predictable latency. We offer monthly reserved SKUs or burst capacity.
- Data retention / SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; default telemetry logs retained 30-45 days for private plans but we can adjust for compliance.
- Contract: attaching term sheet and happy to take procurement redlines.

Propose a short call Thursday (08/06) at 09:30 BST to walk procurement through the sheet and any carve-outs. If that works I'll also invite our Legal (Markus) for quick questions.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivatePlan_TermSheet_v1.docx (DOCX)

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Alliances, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +44 7700 900111

From: CloudWave Procurement <procure@cloudwave.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cloudwave.com>, Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private listing inquiry + initial RFI

Olga — attaching our commercial redlines and a template SOW that our legal team will expect for co-sell engagements. Key asks from Procurement / Legal: 

1) Data retention: require 60 days of retention for access logs and audit trails for regulated customers (financial services).
2) Indemnity / liability cap: prefer uncapped indemnity for IP infringement; cap liability at 2x annual fees for operational issues.
3) Subprocessor / data processing: need flow-down obligations to subprocessors and ability to audit.
4) Marketplace fees: want Redwood to absorb marketplace platform fees for the first 12 months for commercial pilot customers.
5) Revenue split: request 70/30 in favor of CloudWave for the first 12 months; open to revisit after 12 months with joint metrics.

I've attached CW_Redlines_Azure_PrivatePlan_0806.docx with inline legal comments.

Attachments: CW_Redlines_Azure_PrivatePlan_0806.docx (DOCX)

Regards,
CloudWave Procurement
procure@cloudwave.com

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T10:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: CW redlines — urgent legal/commercial review (deal RW-2026-074)

Team — forwarding CloudWave's redlines (see attachment). Procurement is pushing for tougher terms than we usually accept for private marketplace pilots. Summary of asks: 60-day retention, CloudWave wants us to eat marketplace fees for 12 months, and a 70/30 revenue split initially.

Questions:
- Markus: can we accept 45 vs 60 days retention as a compromise? Any material legal exposure on the marketplace-fee absorption ask?
- Laura: from a commercial standpoint, would a 65/35 split + $50k GTM credit for CloudWave in Q1 be acceptable as a counter? Also, is a reserved capacity commit required to justify concessions?

I've flagged the redlines with comments — attaching the CW doc and our term sheet. Need a fast turnaround; procurement wants our position today.

Attachments: CW_Redlines_Azure_PrivatePlan_0806.docx, Redwood_PrivatePlan_TermSheet_v1.docx

— Olga

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T12:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: CW redlines — urgent legal/commercial review (deal RW-2026-074)

Olga / Laura — quick legal read:

- Data retention: we should push back on the 60-day blanket ask. Offer a 45-day default with an option for CloudWave to request a 60-day setting for regulated customers (subject to separate SOW and cost recovery). This limits our exposure but keeps the customer's requirement achievable.
- Indemnity / cap: do not accept uncapped indemnity for IP claims. Counter with a $1M cap for IP and 2x fees for other liabilities; include mutual IP representation.
- Marketplace fees: absorbing Azure's platform fees for 12 months is a material concession. Recommend alternative: Redwood absorbs up to a $X threshold for a defined pilot cohort (e.g., first 5 enterprise seats) or provide a marketing credit equivalent rather than direct fee absorption.
- Revenue split: 70/30 is aggressive. Recommend counter at 65/35 for first 12 months with defined GTM milestones (lead handoff SLAs, co-branded events, pipeline targets). If they commit to reserved capacity or minimum monthly spend (MSP) we can consider 60/40 for the initial term.

I'll prepare tracked changes for our counteroffer and propose language for audit rights and subprocessors.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cloudwave.com>, CloudWave Procurement <procure@cloudwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Azure private listing inquiry + initial RFI — Redwood counter (RW-2026-074)

Matt / Procurement — thanks for the detailed redlines and for the call this morning. We've reviewed internally and here's Redwood's counter in summary (see attached formal counterparty doc):

1) Data retention: Redwood proposes 45 days default for logs/audit data. CloudWave may request a 60-day profile for regulated customers via an SOW; additional retention beyond 45 days would be chargeable.
2) Indemnity / cap: Redwood will provide mutual IP representations and propose a liability cap of $1,000,000 for IP claims, with 2x annual fees for other liabilities.
3) Marketplace fees: rather than absorbing all platform fees, Redwood will provide a $60k marketing/implementation credit for the first 12 months to offset marketplace fees for pilot customers.
4) Revenue split & GTM: Redwood proposes 65/35 (CloudWave 65%) for the first 12 months, moving to a review at month 12 with performance milestones. If CloudWave commits to a reserved capacity minimum (MSP >= $120k ARR) we can consider 60/40 for the initial term.

Next steps:
- Attached: RW_Counter_0807.docx with tracked changes and a summary page.
- If acceptable, we'll issue a DocuSign for signatures (link below).
- Proposed onboarding: once agreements are signed, we will kick off a marketplace SKU creation workflow and technical onboarding; estimated 4 weeks to private listing availability.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/prepare/RW-2026-074
Marketplace onboarding: https://portal.azure.com/marketplace/onboarding/sku-setup/RW-2026-074

Attachments: RW_Counter_0807.docx (DOCX)

Let me know if you want a short commercial-only call today; otherwise we'll await your confirmation on the counter and can circulate the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Alliances, Redwood Inference
